facts.statement: The genus Coloborhynchus was named by Richard Owen in 1874.
facts.quote: authority: Owen, 1874

facts.statement: Coloborhynchus fossils have been found in the Lower Cretaceous of England, dating from 140 to 136 million years ago.
facts.quote: Coloborhynchus is known from the Lower Cretaceous of England (Valanginian age, 140 to 136 million years ago)

facts.statement: Depending on which species are included, Coloborhynchus may also have lived during the Albian and Cenomanian ages, between 113 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: depending on which species are included, possibly the Albian and Cenomanian ages (113 to 93.9 million years ago) as well

facts.statement: Coloborhynchus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur classified within the family Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: Coloborhynchus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur belonging to the family Anhangueridae

facts.statement: Some studies have recovered Coloborhynchus as a member of the family Ornithocheiridae.
facts.quote: though it has also been recovered as a member of the Ornithocheiridae in some studies

facts.statement: Coloborhynchus was once considered the largest known toothed pterosaur, but this record is now held by the closely related genus Tropeognathus.
facts.quote: Coloborhynchus was once thought to be the largest known toothed pterosaur, however, a specimen of the closely related Tropeognathus is now thought to have had a larger wingspan

facts.statement: The genus name Coloborhynchus means "maimed beak," referring to the damaged and eroded condition of the original fossil.
facts.quote: the genus name means "maimed beak", a reference to the damaged and eroded condition of the fossil

facts.statement: The specific name clavirostris means "key snout," referring to the shape of the snout in cross-section.
facts.quote: the specific name means "key snout", referring to its form in cross-section

facts.statement: Richard Owen originally defined the genus by the high position of the front tooth pairs on the side of the upper jaws.
facts.quote: Owen considered the defining trait of the genus to be the location of the front tooth pairs high on the side of the upper jaws

facts.statement: Reginald Walter Hooley argued that the defining jaw trait was an artifact of erosion and that Coloborhynchus was indistinguishable from Criorhynchus simus.
facts.quote: Hooley concluded that this location was an artefact of the erosion and that the genus was indistinguishable from Criorhynchus simus

facts.statement: The genus was revived in 1994 when Yuong-Nam Lee named C. wadleighi based on a snout found in 1992 in the Paw Paw Formation of Texas.
facts.quote: In 1994 when Yuong-Nam Lee named Coloborhynchus wadleighi for a snout found in 1992 in the Albian age Paw Paw Formation Texas

facts.statement: A 2023 review suggested that the traits distinguishing Nicorhynchus from Coloborhynchus were subtle enough to justify synonymizing the two genera.
facts.quote: However, a 2023 review of Kem Kem pterosaurs found the traits that distinguish Nicorhynchus from Coloborhynchus to be subtle enough to justify their synonymy

facts.statement: The final two preserved pairs of teeth in Coloborhynchus pointed downward.
facts.quote: The final two (preserved) pairs of teeth pointed downward.

facts.statement: The rosette at the tip of the Coloborhynchus snout was robust and box-shaped, unlike the rounded and spoon-shaped rosettes of related Anhanguera species.
facts.quote: However, whereas the rosettes of species typically assigned to Anhanguera were rounded and spoon-shaped, those of Coloborhynchus were robust and box-shaped.

facts.statement: The front margin of the Coloborhynchus snout was straight and began at the tip, unlike the curved margins that start further back in related species.
facts.quote: It also had a straight, rather than curved, front margin, unlike its relatives, and begins at the tip of the snout, rather than further back as in other species.

facts.statement: The possible species Coloborhynchus capito is considered the largest known toothed pterosaur and the second largest known ornithocheirid.
facts.quote: The possible species Coloborhynchus capito represents the second largest known ornithocheirid (after a Tropeognathus specimen), and indeed the largest toothed pterosaur known.

facts.statement: If proportions held, a Coloborhynchus capito specimen could have had a skull length of up to 75 cm and an estimated wingspan of 7 meters.
facts.quote: If the proportions of this specimen were consistent with other known species of Coloborhynchus, the total skull length could have been up to 75 cm, leading to an estimated wingspan of 7 m.

facts.statement: Coloborhynchus was a pterodactyloid pterosaur of the family Ornithocheiridae that lived in Europe during the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian), approximately 135 million years ago.
facts.quote: Coloborhynchus es un género de pterosaurios pterodactiloideos de la familia Ornithocheiridae del Cretácico Inferior en Europa (época del Valanginiense, hace 135 millones de años).

facts.statement: A second specimen of Coloborhynchus showing unique features was reported to Alexander Kellner by Darren Naish in 2007, likely representing a second specimen of C. clavirostris that remains undescribed.
facts.quote: A second specimen showing all of these same unique features was reported to Brazilian paleontologist Alexander Kellner by Darren Naish in 2007, and likely represents a second specimen of C. clavirostris, though it has not yet been described.

facts.statement: Many analyses from 2019 and 2020 recovered Coloborhynchus within the family Anhangueridae, specifically in the subfamily Coloborhynchinae.
facts.quote: However, many subsequent analyses made in 2019 and 2020 have recovered Coloborhynchus within the family Anhangueridae, more specifically within the subfamily Coloborhynchinae.

facts.statement: One study classified Coloborhynchus among carnivorous pterosaurs, contrasting with other species classified as piscivores or insectivores.
facts.quote: However one study found it among the carnivorous pterosaur taxa, as opposed to several other piscivore and insectivore species.

facts.statement: The genus Coloborhynchus was originally described by Owen in 1874.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Owen, 1874

facts.statement: According to a 2008 re-evaluation, Coloborhynchus clavirostris can only be differentiated from relatives based on a unique combination of tooth socket positions.
facts.quote: Therefore, according to Rodrigues and Kellner's 2008 re-evaluation on Coloborhynchus clavirostris, it can only be differentiated from its relatives based on its unique combination of tooth socket positions.

facts.statement: Richard Owen named the species Coloborhynchus clavirostris in 1874 based on a partial snout fossil found in the Hastings beds of the Wealden Group in East Sussex, England.
facts.quote: En 1874 Richard Owen, rechazando la creación de Harry Govier Seeley del género Ornithocheirus, nombró las especies Coloborhynchus clavirostris basándose en el holotipo BMNH 1822, un hocico parcial de los lechos de Hastings del Grupo Wealden del Este de Sussex, Inglaterra.

facts.statement: Richard Owen considered the high position of the frontal tooth pairs on the upper jaw side to be the defining characteristic of the genus.
facts.quote: Owen consideró como característica definitoria del género la alta localización de los pares frontales de dientes sobre el lado de la mandíbula superior.

facts.statement: In 1913, Reginald Walter Hooley concluded that the high tooth position was an erosion effect and that the genus was indistinguishable from Criorhynchus simus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 1913 Reginald Walter Hooley concluyó que esta localización era un efecto de la erosión y el género era indistinguible de Criorhynchus simus, el segundo género y especie que Owen designó en 1874.

facts.statement: In 1967, Kuhn agreed with Hooley that Coloborhynchus clavirostris was a synonym of Criorhynchus simus.
facts.quote: En 1967, Kuhn estuvo de acuerdo con Hooley en que Coloborhynchus clavirostris era un sinónimo de Criorhynchus simus.

facts.statement: The genus was resurrected in 1994 when Yuong-Nam Lee named Coloborhynchus wadleighi based on a snout found in 1992 in the Paw Paw Formation of Texas, from the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Esto cambió en 1994, cuando Yuong-Nam Lee nombró a Coloborhynchus wadleighi de un hocico hallado en 1992 en la formación Paw Paw de Texas, del Albiense.

facts.statement: In 2008, Taissa Rodrigues and Alexander Kellner reformulated the characteristics of Coloborhynchus, basing them mainly on the unique positions of the tooth sockets.
facts.quote: En 2008, Taissa Rodrigues y Alexander Kellner reformularon las características de Coloborhynchus, de nuevo basándose mayormente en las posiciones únicas de los alvéolos de los dientes.

facts.statement: Rodrigues and Kellner argued that C. wadleighi, which has differences in the skull and teeth compared to C. clavirostris and comes from an earlier period, belongs to its own genus, which they named Uktenadactylus.
facts.quote: Rodrigues y Kellner afirmó que el C. wadleighi de Lee, que posee algunas diferencias en el cráneo y dientes respecto a C. clavirostris, y proviene de un período anterior, pertenecía a su propio género, el cual nombraron Uktenadactylus.

facts.statement: In 2001, Fastnacht assigned a partial lower jaw originally named Tropeognathus robustus from the Romualdo Member of the Santana Formation in Brazil to Coloborhynchus as C. robustus.
facts.quote: Una mandíbula inferior parcial originalmente denominada Tropeognathus robustus del Miembro Romualdo de la formación Santana en Brasil fue asignada a Coloborhycnhus en 2001 por Fastnacht, como Coloborhynchus robustus.

facts.statement: In 2002, David Unwin supported this idea and also synonymized the well-known species Anhanguera piscator with C. robustus.
facts.quote: En 2002, David Unwin apoyó esta idea, y también sinonimizó a la bien conocida especie Anhanguera piscator con C. robustus.

facts.statement: Rodrigues and Kellner disagreed with this classification, noting that both lacked the straight crest starting at the snout tip or teeth pointing to the sides as seen in C. clavirostris.
facts.quote: Rodrigues y Kellner no estuvieron de acuerdo con esa clasificación, notando que ambos no poseían la cresta recta en la punta del hocico comenzando en la punta del hocico, o dientes apuntando a los lados, como en C. clavirostris.

facts.statement: In 2003, paleontologist André Veldmeijer named Coloborhynchus spielbergi after studying a specimen cataloged as C. robustus from the Naturalis Museum in the Netherlands, honoring Steven Spielberg with the species name.
facts.quote: Otra especie brasileña del Miembro Romualdo fue nombrada Coloborhynchus spielbergi por el paleontólogo André Veldmeijer en 2003, al estudiar un ejemplar catalogado como C. robustus del museo Naturalis de Holanda, al que determinó como una nueva especie de Coloborhynchus, cuyo nombre de especie, C. spielbergi, fue dado en honor a Steven Spielberg.

facts.statement: C. spielbergi would reach a wingspan of 6 meters.
facts.quote: Alcanzaría 6 m de envergadura.

facts.statement: In 2001, Unwin assigned the species Siroccopteryx moroccensis to Coloborhynchus based on its similarity to C. wadleighi (i.e., Uktenadactylus).
facts.quote: Unwin, en 2001, asignó a la especie Siroccopteryx moroccensis a Coloborhycnhus, basándose en su similitud a C. wadleighi (es decir, Uktenadactylus).

facts.statement: Kellner, who considered Uktenadactylus a distinct genus in 2008, also considered Siroccopteryx different, noting it lacked the unique dental row characteristics of Coloborhynchus, a view supported by Fastnacht in 2001.
facts.quote: Kellner, quien consideró a Uktenadactylus como un género distinto en 2008, también considera a Siroccopteryx como diferente, y notó que como otras especies asignadas a Coloborhynchus, carecía de sus características únicas de la fila dental, una postura apoyada por Fastnacht en 2001.

facts.statement: Finally, Unwin (in 2001) also reassigned two other species from the Cambridge Greensand to Coloborhynchus: C. capito and C. sedgwickii, the latter being one of the original genus members according to Richard Owen in 1874.
facts.quote: Finalmente, Unwin (en 2001) también reasignó a otras dos especies de Cambridge Greensand a Coloborhycnhus: C. capito y C. sedgwickii, la segunda de las cuales es uno de los miembros originales del género de acuerdo a Richard Owen en 1874.

facts.statement: According to Kellner, C. capito is too incomplete for a full comparison with C. clavirostris, and its precise classification remains open to debate.
facts.quote: De acuerdo a Kellner, C. capito es muy incompleto como para realizar una comparación completa con C. clavirostris, y su clasificación precisa está abierta a debate.

facts.statement: He noted that C. sedgwickii lacks the unique characteristics of C. clavirostris (in fact, it completely lacks a crest) and may even belong to the same genus as "Ornithocheirus" compressirostris (=Lonchodectes).
facts.quote: Él señaló que C. sedgwicki no posee las características únicas de C. clavirostris (de hecho carece completamente de una cresta), y puede incluso pertenecer al mismo género que "Ornithocheirus" compressirostris (=Lonchodectes).
